thread:
Sam (new-hire): hey team, day 1 gotcha. I'm on an Ubuntu laptop at a coworking space, using the onboarding WireGuard split-tunnel profile. SSH to bastion drops after a few minutes and `git clone` sometimes fails with DNS errors. I also noticed my machine resolves gitlab.redwood to an IPv6 address randomly. anyone seen ipv6 + split-tunnel weirdness?

Nina (infra): welcome! yep, IPv6 can leak to the public resolver if WG only routes IPv4 internal subnets. Short TCP sessions + DNS flip = disconnects. First things: share your ~/.ssh/config for bastion (no secrets) and check `systemd-resolved` status.

Sam (new-hire): here's the ssh host entry:```
Host bastion.cowork
  HostName bastion.us-east-1.redwood
  User sam
  ProxyCommand ssh -W %h:%p jump.redwood
```

Ollie (it-support): two quick fixes: 1) switch ProxyCommand -> ProxyJump and add ServerAliveInterval 25; 2) make sure WireGuard config forces internal DNS and disables IPv6 routing for internal hosts. On Ubuntu, systemd-resolved sometimes prefers public IPv6 answers; pin the internal resolver by creating /etc/systemd/resolved.conf.d/redwood.conf with `DNS=10.0.4.2` and `FallbackDNS=` then `systemctl restart systemd-resolved`.

Nina (infra): add these ssh lines too:```
  ProxyJump jump.redwood
  ServerAliveInterval 25
  ServerAliveCountMax 3
```
Also run `sudo sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1` as a quick repro to see if IPv6 is the culprit (not a permanent fix). If that removes the DNS flips, we'll update the WG profile to explicitly disable IPv6 for internal nets.

deploy-bot: scheduled rolling reboot: bastion-cowork-1 rebooting in 5m for kernel updates (maint-2026-09-02-1). Sessions on that host may be interrupted.

Sam (new-hire): ok I switched to ProxyJump and added ServerAliveInterval. I also created the resolved conf and restarted systemd-resolved. Still saw one drop exactly during the maintenance window but DNS resolves are stable now and git clones work (no more IPv6 answers).

Ollie (it-support): great. we'll update the onboarding WG profile to set DNS=10.0.4.2 and add a note to disable IPv6 for internal resolution on Linux laptops or ensure the client advertises no IPv6 for internal subnets. Adding a short troubleshooting step to the new-hire doc: "If dns resolution returns public IPv6 addresses, force internal resolver or temporarily disable IPv6."

Sam (new-hire): perfect, thanks for the help and quick responses!
